slides.title: Introduction
slides.subtitle: Building got cheap. Knowing what to build, and making it legible, did not.

slides.title: Same task. Half of them got Copilot.
slides.lead: A controlled experiment at Microsoft Research in 2022. One task, two groups, one tool handed to one side.
slides.why: the chapter opens on a controlled experiment: identical developers, identical task, split at the moment half are handed Copilot, landing on 71 minutes versus 161 — a shared origin that separates at a named moment

slides.title: When building gets cheap, building stops being the scarce skill
slides.lead: That 56% collapse is not a productivity story. It is a signaling story — and signaling is branding.
bullets: The scarce skill is knowing **what** to build.
And making that work **legible** to the people it is for.
*That is a branding problem.* This book teaches brand strategy for technical practitioners whose credentials no longer separate them.
With AI as your tool — **not your replacement**.

slides.title: Ideate · Build · Brand · Ship
slides.lead: A graduate-level, hands-on branding course. It reads the cheapening of technical signals through Spence's signaling mechanism and names the four verbs that now carry career value.
bullets: The brand disciplines that make a **Creative Engineer** recognizable: archetype, scope, pipelines, interface, positioning, visual identity, storytelling, portfolio, launch.
Every chapter opens on a **brand decision**, then uses AI to execute it.
What it is *not*: a tour of AI tools. The tool changes every quarter; the brand decision does not.
When a chapter reaches for AI, **the decision leads and the model follows.**

slides.section: the idea running through the book
slides.title: AI+1 — the agent drafts, you own the decision
slides.lead: The division of labor is the whole argument. AI is excellent at reformatting, drafting, and pattern-spotting — and unreliable at the calibrated, accountable judgments brand work turns on.
slides.why: the chapter draws an explicit permission boundary — the agent drafts; you, the +1, own committing an archetype, approving a voice, signing off a position, accepting a persona as real, clearing a claim

attempts.label: hand you a draft to check

slides.title: Madison: this book ships the AI it teaches you to use
slides.lead: The `madison/` directory is a self-contained copy of the Madison framework — an open-source, agent-based marketing-intelligence system.
bullets: Organized into **five agent roles plus orchestration**.
Download the repository and the end-of-chapter exercises are runnable. No other clone required.
Madison is the *tool*. This book is the *branding course* that uses it.
Anything the agent generates — a persona, a metric, a citation — is a draft that needs an evidence check.

slides.title: Twelve chapters, each opening on a decision
slides.lead: Signal, framework, archetype, scope, pipelines, intelligence, interface, strategy, identity, story, portfolio, launch.
bullets: **Ch 4 — the $100,000 no.** What you refuse to build defines the product.
**Ch 5 — every external dependency is a contract**, and every contract will change.
**Ch 10 — a brand telling the wrong story burns faster than none.**

slides.title: At Chapter 8 you pick a path and carry it to the end
slides.lead: Positioning as a defensible claim, on two tracks you choose between — or run both.
slides.why: the chapter names a literal fork: 'At Chapter 8, pick the path that fits — personal (8a) or startup (8b) — and carry it to the end'

tracks.label: 8a · Personal Brand Path
notes: the Creative Engineer as the claim

slides.title: The chapters compound — and the thread returns to you
slides.lead: Read in order if the field is new. Each chapter's artifact is the next chapter's input.
slides.why: the chapter states an explicit dependency chain: 'your Chapter 1 signal baseline feeds your Chapter 3 audience, which feeds your Chapter 4 scope, and so on to the Chapter 12 launch' — which returns to you

slides.section: what this deck does not tell you
slides.title: The Self-as-Project thread is yours to run
slides.lead: Every chapter closes with a five-part AI+1 block that advances your own brand by running the mapped Madison recipe.
bullets: Whether your signal baseline holds, whether your archetype survives contact, whether your claim clears an evidence check — **TO RUN**.

The chapter states one experiment: 71 minutes against 161, a 56% collapse. So that is the only figure this deck states. The grey slot in the chain is the part the chapter writes as *and so on* — you fill it.
Generic copy, fabricated personas, and unprovable claims are exactly what destroy a brand at first contact.

slides.title: Building got cheap. Deciding did not.
slides.lead: Pick the brand you will run end to end. Open Chapter 1, set your signal baseline, and own every judgment the agent hands you. Let's go.
